sections.title: Reading images
sections.lede: Header-only reads and full decodes, from bytes and from a file, on every corpus entry: synthetic images of four shapes and real photographs, each stored as png, jpg, bmp and tga.

ops.title: info: read the header only, no pixels
ops.note: Width, height and channel count without decoding anything. Only libstb and Pillow have a header-only call; OpenCV and imageio do not, so they are absent here.

ops.title: decode: encoded bytes in, pixel array out
ops.note: Each file was written by Pillow, never by stb. OpenCV has no TGA decoder, so it has no TGA entries. imageio delegates to Pillow, so it is Pillow plus its own overhead.

ops.title: load_file: path in, pixel array out
ops.note: The same as decode but starting from a path, so file I/O is included: what someone actually types.

sections.title: Writing images
sections.lede: Raw pixels to file bytes, at matched settings. Speed alone is not the whole story for an encoder, so each panel also shows how large the output is.

ops.title: encode PNG: raw pixels in, file bytes out
ops.note: zlib level 6 on every side. stb bundles its own small deflate instead of zlib, so the same level does not produce the same bytes: read the speed together with the output-size table.

ops.title: encode JPEG: raw pixels in, file bytes out
ops.note: Quality 90 on every side, 3-channel images only. Encoders make different size/quality trades at the same setting, so the output-size table matters as much as the time.

ops.title: encode BMP: raw pixels in, file bytes out
ops.note: Uncompressed, so this is mostly memory bandwidth. 3-channel images only.

ops.title: encode TGA: raw pixels in, file bytes out
ops.note: Uncompressed on every side (libstb with rle=False, matching Pillow's default). OpenCV has no TGA encoder.

sections.title: Resizing images
sections.lede: Half size and double size, with linear, cubic and box filters.

ops.title: resize, half size, linear (triangle)
ops.note: libstb, Pillow and scikit-image prefilter when shrinking; OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR and INTER_CUBIC do not (faster, and they alias), and INTER_AREA is its antialiasing counterpart. "libstb" is Resizer(filter, srgb=False), the like-for-like pairing; "libstb (sRGB-correct)" is the library's own default, which blends in linear light like a correct resizer should, listed separately so the price of that is visible. 3-channel images only. scikit-image is skipped above 1 MP (seconds per call).

ops.title: resize, half size, cubic (Catmull-Rom)
ops.note: libstb, Pillow and scikit-image prefilter when shrinking; OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR and INTER_CUBIC do not (faster, and they alias), and INTER_AREA is its antialiasing counterpart. "libstb" is Resizer(filter, srgb=False), the like-for-like pairing; "libstb (sRGB-correct)" is the library's own default, which blends in linear light like a correct resizer should, listed separately so the price of that is visible. 3-channel images only. scikit-image is skipped above 1 MP (seconds per call).

ops.title: resize, half size, box / area
ops.note: libstb, Pillow and scikit-image prefilter when shrinking; OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR and INTER_CUBIC do not (faster, and they alias), and INTER_AREA is its antialiasing counterpart. "libstb" is Resizer(filter, srgb=False), the like-for-like pairing; "libstb (sRGB-correct)" is the library's own default, which blends in linear light like a correct resizer should, listed separately so the price of that is visible. 3-channel images only. scikit-image is skipped above 1 MP (seconds per call). scikit-image has no box filter.

ops.title: resize, double size, linear (triangle)
ops.note: libstb, Pillow and scikit-image prefilter when shrinking; OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR and INTER_CUBIC do not (faster, and they alias), and INTER_AREA is its antialiasing counterpart. "libstb" is Resizer(filter, srgb=False), the like-for-like pairing; "libstb (sRGB-correct)" is the library's own default, which blends in linear light like a correct resizer should, listed separately so the price of that is visible. 3-channel images only. scikit-image is skipped above 1 MP (seconds per call).

ops.title: resize, double size, cubic (Catmull-Rom)
ops.note: libstb, Pillow and scikit-image prefilter when shrinking; OpenCV's INTER_LINEAR and INTER_CUBIC do not (faster, and they alias), and INTER_AREA is its antialiasing counterpart. "libstb" is Resizer(filter, srgb=False), the like-for-like pairing; "libstb (sRGB-correct)" is the library's own default, which blends in linear light like a correct resizer should, listed separately so the price of that is visible. 3-channel images only. scikit-image is skipped above 1 MP (seconds per call).

sections.title: Editing images
sections.lede: Crop, quarter turn, flip, RGB to gray and alpha compositing: the operations libstb added for working on pixels without leaving the library, against Pillow and OpenCV where they have one.

ops.title: crop: the central half of each side
ops.note: A new, independent image in every library (an OpenCV slice is a view, so it is copied). This is mostly memory bandwidth. 3-channel images only.

ops.title: rotate: a counter-clockwise quarter turn
ops.note: Pillow's transpose(ROTATE_90) and cv2.rotate against libstb's rotate90. A turn reads rows and writes columns, so it is about memory access patterns. 3-channel images only.

ops.title: flip left to right
ops.note: Pillow's transpose(FLIP_LEFT_RIGHT) and cv2.flip against libstb's flip_horizontal. 3-channel images only.

ops.title: convert: RGB to gray
ops.note: libstb and Pillow use the same integer formula and give identical pixels; OpenCV's BGR2GRAY rounds slightly differently. libstb runs the fastest SIMD backend of the CPU it is measured on (libstb.simd_name()). 3-channel images only.

ops.title: composite: RGBA over RGBA, straight alpha
ops.note: An RGBA image laid over its own upside-down copy, against Pillow's Image.alpha_composite (OpenCV has no equivalent). The alpha channel is identical; the colour is within one level where the pixel is visible. 4-channel images only, so only the graphics images take part.

ops.title: open: load the font file, get a font object
measure: how big would this text be
render: text in, coverage bitmap out (measure + allocate + draw)

install.label: libstb
install.capability: image decode, png/jpg/bmp/tga encode, resize, TrueType text (stb, no system dependencies)

install.label: Pillow
install.capability: many-format image io, resize, filters, drawing, FreeType text

install.label: numpy
install.capability: arrays only (a dependency of OpenCV, imageio and scikit-image; optional for libstb, not used by Pillow)

install.label: imageio
install.capability: many-format image io (delegates to Pillow and friends)

install.label: scikit-image
install.capability: image processing algorithms (io + resize + far more)

install.label: OpenCV
install.capability: image io, resize, and a large computer-vision toolkit
